gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Vapcell S4+ can run 3 A in all four slots because it is powered from a 12 V DC adapter (lygte-info measured about 4.5 A from 12 V with four cells at 3 A, roughly 54 W), while the USB-C-powered XTARs are limited to an 18 to 20 W input and drop to 1 A per cell with four 18650s loaded.
standout_why: I compared against 1lumen VC4SL (cited), m0mnf VC4SL (cited), timmcmahon VX4 (cited) and the xtar.cc comparison page. 1lumen already says single-cell 3 A 'is the most you can get from QC3's 18W power' and gives the 3A/2A/1A split. Both ChatGPT answers repeat that split. Tim McMahon gives the VX4's PD 20 W (12V/1.67A) input. None of these pages put the USB power ceiling side by side with the Vapcell's 12 V brick or with a measured input draw for four cells at 3 A. ChatGPT's 'up to 3A per slot simultaneously' line for the Vapcell had no power figure behind it. I could not open the cited manuals.plus Vapcell manual (HTTP 403), so it may state the adapter rating.
decides: If the shopper wants to charge four 18650s fast, only a charger with a DC brick (the Vapcell S4 Plus) can push 3 A into each cell. A USB-C XTAR (VC4SL or VX4) charges four cells at 1 A each, because 4 × 3 A × 4.2 V is about 50 W against an 18 to 20 W USB input. For one or two cells the XTARs are just as fast. Dealectric's listed Tenergy TN270 charges at 500 mA per slot, which is the slow, gentle end.

findings.label: Charge power at 3 A per 18650 near full voltage
findings.value: about 12.6 W per cell; about 50 W for four cells
findings.note: Arithmetic: 3 A × 4.2 V (the 1lumen-measured end voltage was 4.19 V) = 12.6 W, × 4 = 50.4 W. Converter losses are not counted.

findings.label: Input and current split by number of cells
findings.value: USB-C QC3.0, 5V 3A / 9V 2A; 3 A × 1, 2 A × 2, 1 A × 4; 2 A from a regular USB-A port
findings.note: 1lumen: 'requires a USB-C source with QC, supplying around 18W'. It measured 3060 mA into a 3000 mAh 18650 (1.2 h) and a 10440 was automatically cut to 260 mA.

findings.label: Input per maker
findings.value: QC3.0 (5V 3A / 9V 2A) via USB-C; internal resistance check: Yes; low-voltage activation: Yes
findings.source_title: XTAR Charger Comparison: VX4 VS. VC4SL VS. VP4L PLUS - XTAR
findings.note: Spec table on XTAR's own page.

findings.label: Input per maker
findings.value: PD2.0 (12V 1.67A) / QC3.0 (9V 2A) / 5V 2A via USB-C; internal resistance check: No; manual current up to 3 A
findings.source_title: XTAR Charger Comparison: VX4 VS. VC4SL VS. VP4L PLUS - XTAR

findings.label: Current split, input dependence and cut-off
findings.value: 3A×1 / 2A×2 / 1A×4; 20 W PD (12V/1.67A) recommended; QC3 (9V/2A) and 5V/2A 'will work but the charging current might be limited'; cut-off 4.2±0.05 V, ≤150 mA
findings.source_title: XTAR VX4 Charger Review :: Tim McMahon
findings.note: Tim McMahon selected 3000 mA on a Sanyo NCR18650GA and the VX4 charged at 500 mA. He thinks his shunt may have raised the internal resistance the charger measured.

findings.label: Input adapter and measured draw with four cells at 3 A
findings.value: 12 V 3 A adapter (100-240 VAC); about 4.5 A drawn from 12 V with four cells at 3 A (about 54 W)
findings.note: lygte-info does not name the hardware revision, so this may not be the V3.0. 12 V × 4.5 A = 54 W, which is more than the 36 W the 3 A adapter is rated for.

findings.label: Termination and low-voltage handling (measured)
findings.value: about 100 mA termination at the 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 3 A settings; 200 mA pre-charge below 3.0 V; error reported below 0.4 V; does not restart when a full cell's voltage drops
findings.note: Measured by HKJ (lygte-info.dk). Revision not stated.

findings.label: Output, charge rate and price
findings.value: 4.2 V, 500 mA × 2 independent channels; 500 mA for 18650 and 14500; AC 100-240 V input; $18.99, in stock
findings.source_title: Tenergy TN270 Li-ion 18650/18500/14500 Fast Battery Charger
findings.note: Maker's US product page. The page does not state the termination method, 0 V handling or accepted cell length. Its package-contents list says 'TN271'.
